title: Clarify error behavior when a document becomes inactive while requestLEScan() or requestDevice() is pending prompt display
body:
When [`navigator.bluetooth.requestLEScan()`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/scanning.html#dom-bluetooth-requestlescan)  or [`navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice()`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-bluetooth-requestdevice) is invoked, several steps run **in parallel** before the user agent displays a permission prompt or device chooser (for example, acquiring/initializing the platform Bluetooth adapter or starting a discovery session).

If the requesting `Document` becomes no longer [fully active](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#fully-active) during these asynchronous steps (before the permission prompt is shown), the user agent cannot display UI prompts for that document and must abort the request.

Currently, the specification defines how to handle an active scan when a document loses activity (e.g., [§ 4.1 Controlling a BLE scan](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/scanning.html#scan-control)), but does not explicitly specify how `requestLEScan()` or `requestDevice()` should reject the returned promise when a document was active at invocation time, but became inactive before the prompt could be shown:

- In [`requestLEScan(options)`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/scanning.html#dom-bluetooth-requestlescan):
  - **Step 9.1** ([request permission to use](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/scanning.html#scanning-permission)) runs in parallel and may require transient activation on the relevant global object.
  - **Step 9.4.1** specifies that if the UA failed to start scanning, it must reject `promise` with:
    - `"NotSupportedError"` if the UA doesn't support scanning for advertisements
    - `"InvalidStateError"` if Bluetooth is turned off
    - `"UnknownError"` for other reasons
- In [`requestDevice(options)`](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-bluetooth-requestdevice):
  - **Step 4.1** invokes [request Bluetooth devices](https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#request-bluetooth-devices) in parallel, which checks transient user activation in **Step 4** and later prompts the user to select a device, without specifying what exception to throw if `document` is no longer fully active when the chooser is about to be shown.

Should the specification explicitly check whether `document` is still **fully active** before displaying permission prompts in `requestLEScan()` and `requestDevice()`, and define the expected `DOMException` name when it is not (e.g., `UnknownError`, `InvalidStateError`, or `AbortError`)?
